description: NL->SQL questions over the `weather` dataset (public/data/datasets.json): weather(time TIMESTAMP hourly UTC, city VARCHAR (12), country VARCHAR (10), temperature, humidity, precipitation, wind_speed, cloud_cover, pressure DOUBLE), 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-31, 210,528 rows. Real data (ERA5 via Open-Meteo). Same rules as evals/sql-corpus.json: executed results are compared, several references mean several acceptable readings, $SINCE(n unit) expands on the `time` column.

cases.question: average temperature per city
cases.reference: SELECT city, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

cases.question: what was the highest temperature
reference: SELECT max(temperature) AS max_temperature FROM weather
SELECT time, city, temperature FROM weather ORDER BY temperature DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT city, time, temperature FROM weather ORDER BY temperature DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT city, max(temperature) AS max_temperature FROM weather GROUP BY city ORDER BY max_temperature DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: total precipitation per city in 2024
cases.reference: SELECT city, sum(precipitation) AS precipitation FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

cases.question: monthly average temperature in Berlin
cases.reference: SELECT date_trunc('month', time) AS month, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather WHERE city = 'Berlin' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

cases.question: daily maximum temperature in Madrid over the last 30 days
cases.reference: SELECT date_trunc('day', time) AS day, max(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather WHERE city = 'Madrid' AND $SINCE(30 days) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

cases.question: hourly wind speed in Copenhagen over the last 2 days
cases.reference: SELECT time, wind_speed FROM weather WHERE city = 'Copenhagen' AND $SINCE(2 days) ORDER BY time
cases.note: The data is already hourly: no aggregation needed, but time_bucket + avg gives the same values.

cases.question: which city is the coldest on average
reference: SELECT city, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather GROUP BY city ORDER BY temperature LIMIT 1
SELECT city FROM weather GROUP BY city ORDER BY avg(temperature) LIMIT 1
SELECT city, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather GROUP BY city ORDER BY temperature

cases.question: top 5 windiest hours in Oslo
reference: SELECT time, wind_speed FROM weather WHERE city = 'Oslo' ORDER BY wind_speed DESC, time LIMIT 5
SELECT time, wind_speed FROM weather WHERE city = 'Oslo' ORDER BY wind_speed DESC, time DESC LIMIT 5
cases.note: Ties at 36.2 (3rd/4th) and 35.9 (5th/6th): either tie order is accepted.

cases.question: number of hours with rain per city
reference: SELECT city, count(*) FILTER (WHERE precipitation > 0) AS rainy_hours FROM weather GROUP BY city ORDER BY city
SELECT city, count(*) AS rainy_hours FROM weather WHERE precipitation > 0 GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

cases.question: average humidity by country
cases.reference: SELECT country, avg(humidity) AS humidity FROM weather GROUP BY country ORDER BY country

cases.question: average temperature by hour of day

SELECT date_trunc('day', time) AS day, avg(temperature) FILTER (WHERE city = 'Berlin') AS berlin, avg(temperature) FILTER (WHERE city = 'London') AS london FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT city, count(*) AS freezing_hours FROM weather WHERE temperature <= 0 AND time >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

cases.question: which month of 2024 was the warmest in each city
reference: SELECT city, arg_max(month, temperature) AS warmest_month FROM (SELECT city, date_trunc('month', time) AS month, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY ALL) GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

SELECT city, arg_max(month, temperature) AS warmest_month, max(temperature) AS temperature FROM (SELECT city, date_trunc('month', time) AS month, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY ALL) GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

SELECT city, arg_max(month, temperature) AS warmest_month FROM (SELECT city, month(time) AS month, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY ALL) GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

SELECT city, arg_max(month, temperature) AS warmest_month, max(temperature) AS temperature FROM (SELECT city, month(time) AS month, avg(temperature) AS temperature FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY ALL) GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

cases.question: how many hours had wind above 50 km/h, per city

SELECT city, count(*) FILTER (WHERE wind_speed > 50) AS hours FROM weather GROUP BY city ORDER BY city

cases.question: Longest dry streak in hours (consecutive hours without precipitation) per city
cases.reference: WITH w AS (SELECT city, precipitation = 0 AS dry, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY time) - row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY city, precipitation = 0 ORDER BY time) AS grp FROM weather), s AS (SELECT city, grp, count(*) AS n FROM w WHERE dry GROUP BY ALL) SELECT city, max(n) AS hours FROM s GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

cases.question: monthly average temperature of each city relative to that city's overall average
reference: SELECT date_trunc('month', time) AS month, city, avg(temperature) - avg(avg(temperature)) OVER (PARTITION BY city) AS anomaly FROM weather GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

SELECT date_trunc('month', w.time) AS month, w.city, avg(w.temperature) - c.m AS anomaly FROM weather w JOIN (SELECT city, avg(temperature) AS m FROM weather GROUP BY 1) c USING (city) GROUP BY 1, 2, c.m ORDER BY 1, 2
cases.note: Relative to the mean of the monthly means or of all hours.

cases.question: per city, how many days had a daily maximum temperature above that city's 90th percentile of daily maxima
reference: WITH d AS (SELECT city, date_trunc('day', time) AS day, max(temperature) AS t FROM weather GROUP BY ALL), p AS (SELECT city, quantile_cont(t, 0.9) AS p90 FROM d GROUP BY 1) SELECT city, count(*) AS days FROM d JOIN p USING (city) WHERE t > p90 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH d AS (SELECT city, date_trunc('day', time) AS day, max(temperature) AS t FROM weather GROUP BY ALL), p AS (SELECT city, quantile_disc(t, 0.9) AS p90 FROM d GROUP BY 1) SELECT city, count(*) AS days FROM d JOIN p USING (city) WHERE t > p90 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

cases.question: share of each city's 2024 precipitation that fell on its single wettest day
reference: WITH d AS (SELECT city, date_trunc('day', time) AS day, sum(precipitation) AS p FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY ALL) SELECT city, max(p) / sum(p) AS share FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH d AS (SELECT city, date_trunc('day', time) AS day, sum(precipitation) AS p FROM weather WHERE time >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND time < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' GROUP BY ALL) SELECT city, 100 * max(p) / sum(p) AS share FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
